verdict.tagline: Brutal dinosaur survival marred by technical hurdles and severe progress loss.
for_you_if: you want a harsh dinosaur survival sandbox
you can handle losing hours of progress
you enjoy playing with groups in open worlds
not_for_you_if: you cannot tolerate losing hours of progress on death
you need stable servers without lag or crashes
you are unwilling to opt into beta branches

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks a tutorial, map, or clear in-game instructions explaining controls and mechanics.

citations.review_text:
I wanted to play this game with my girlfriend, and somehow we didn't even make it to the dinosaur part. She couldn't properly load into the game, and before we could even start building a nest, surviving together, or doing anything fun, we were already fighting with the game itself. A game where you can literally mate and create a dinosaur family somehow defeated us before we even got there.

I saw this game online and honestly thought it looked incredible. The idea is amazing. You are a dinosaur. That is basically the peak male experience. I wanted to jump in, pick a dinosaur, meet up with my girlfriend, explore the world, roar at everything, and just have a relaxing prehistoric adventure.

Instead, I spent my first 30 minutes trying to understand how the game even works.

The spawn code system is confusing. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. I managed to get in, but then the map didn't even load properly. The biggest issue is that the spawn code only helps during the first few minutes after you spawn. Once you are already in the world, you cannot change dinosaur anymore. You are stuck with your choice.

So if you and your friend spawn in completely different areas, good luck. You have to run toward each other across a huge map, with no proper in-game map to help you. I understand the immersion argument. Dinosaurs didn't have maps, GPS, or a minimap showing where they were. I actually like the idea of making you feel like an animal.

But there is a difference between immersive and frustrating.

Having to use an external website, pause the game, check coordinates, and manually figure out where you are feels unnecessary. The game already has a scent system to help you navigate, and while the idea is cool, it is not something that feels natural for a new player.

The biggest problem is that the game explains almost nothing. When you launch it, you basically get a menu where you press play, join a server, and that's it. There is no proper tutorial, no explanatio…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks an in-game tutorial or guides, requiring players to use external sources like Google or third-party sites to understand mechanics, controls, maps, and specific dinosaur abilities.

citations.review_text:
So far, I love this game. 

My partner and I have been playing on PvE servers with like, at least 10+ other players. This has been the most reward, as we tried dead servers at first and felt a little lonely. The server we are on has a discord with a map extension so we can find eachother. It's really helpful!

There is quite a learning curve at first, each dino has different abilities, so i def recommend googling the dino your'e playing as and just playing around with it before getting attached to your character. You'll find your favorites if you approach it casually and just play around (: 

The community aspect of this game is super fun and cute. I love running along, approaching other players, saying hello, sharing food, etc. the RP aspect of this game is my favorite part of the game I suppose! 

And to be clear, one of my all time favorite games IS The Binding of Isaac; perma death doesn't scare me, lol.

If you're intrigued by this game but unsure if you have the mental fortitude to try it, wait for it to go on sale. If you're super intrigued and wanna be a fweakin' dina-saw, get the fweakin gaym. <3

I chose yes because the option is binary. I'd have chosen "Maybe" if I could. 

  It is a good attempt at a wildlife simulator. I like lounging in the river as a pre-historic crocodile. However, it needs the backing of a proper team that gives it their full time attention. 

  As a game it is at its best, barely playable. Frame-rate jumps and drops, light and textures not properly loading. Your animal sometimes spawning in the ground. Most of the time there is barely anything else or anyone forever even on full servers. There is no information for how anything functions. Which is a massive problem because how else are you supposed to gather and process the information about your environment in order to hunt, hide and survive in a game where the entire goal is to hunt, hide and survive? 

  And despite all this it is nothing short of amazing. I cannot express to you how long my heart has been waiting for the opportunity to just play a dumb animal living in its environment. Again; I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love just laying around at the edge of a river until my crocodile guy or girl is hungry or thirsty or I just feel like moving. Interacting with the eco-system. Hearing and contributing to the cacophony of calls. Its wonderful really. Somewhere I'm positive I can hear Werner Herzog complain about the fornication and death. 

  Please start a crowd-funding for this game so we can donate enough money to hire the staff to work the game full time and hire more developers. This game really deserves to be fully realized. Despite its flaws there is NOTHING, I mean nothing even remotely like it right now.

This is a very fun simulation of dinosaur game. I especially like the voice servers which can be very entertaining. The Downside to the game, is there isn't very much of a tutorial on game play. but can be figured out by researching or looking up the controls I guess. I also did notice that it can be a bit buggy but nothing to crazy in my opinion.

I've been playing this game with my kid, and I know it's early access, but the fact that I had to do some internet diving to discover that to even play I had to be on evrima is a bit much. Why the official servers were abandoned is beyond me.

Spawn codes, while useful, don't always seem to work.

Implement a way to delete your dino from a server without having to just die. If I'm playing with a friend, and we've linked into a group but one of us dies, we'd like to restart together without having to switch servers. So then one of us is stuck waiting for the other dino to commit suicide so we can start over together again.

I am a huge newbie with large online server-based games. I thought I would get eaten right away, and sure enough I did as a medium sized herbivore. I'm not stressing if I lose a dino right away since it is about survival, even on an unofficial server provided by other community members. I liked getting the hang of controls as a hypsi aka the tiny chicken, and getting a few steps in before trying anything else. It is pretty helpful being with at least one other friend to help you spot potential threats, search for food or water, get the hang of the controls etc.. I will admit controls could be easier to decipher but be careful due to live interactions while perusing the menu options. The path to mutations and what entombing is didn't make sense, as there's plenty more to learn before I 100% any dino, so thank goodness for google. And with that I recommend searching for The Isle for Beginners. great threads explaining a lot. And find a community!

THE GOOD: 
-There is a pretty diverse selection of dinosaurs to choose from.
-The map is very large and there are a lot of different kinds of foods located everywhere throughout.
THE NEUTRAL: 
-The customization options are very limited and for the most part you can choose between a few shades of brown.
-You will need to google a lot of things in terms of mechanics and symbols because there's no guides or tutorials or even a map or anything.
THE BAD:
-You mature until you are at 100% and then what? Apparently there is an evolution system but I can't for the life of me figure out how to evolve and I can't find any relevant guides so after I mature to 100% and entomb myself I am transported to an un-loaded void until I eventually get bored and log out. (If anyone can tell me what I'm actually meant to do after entombment that would be greatly appreciated!)
-It is very boring if there aren't a lot of players around. You move from place to place to eat and drink but there's not much else.
-The controls are very finicky and a little buggy when it comes to eating and drinking and I have on average had to try about 3 times from different angles in order to eat or drink.
-Sometimes at night it becomes nearly impossible to see, and night vision doesn't really help. I know it's supposed to be a handicap that makes the experience more immersive but it makes the game borderline unplayable.
I like the mechanics but definitely read up on how to play first

citations.review_text: Best game ever designed. Maps, dinos, battles and community are awesome. Sadly it is unplayable in my pc. 2 crashes in 4 hours means i cant get involved in the game as intended.

Landing is not a skill—it's a suggestion.

I learned that having wings doesn't make you safe. It just means you have more dramatic ways to die.

Every flight was either:

* "Wow, this game is beautiful."
* "I think I'm finally safe."
* "OH NO."
* *You have died.*

10/10 survival experience. The biggest predator wasn't another dinosaur—it was my own terrible flying skills.

Would become an airborne panic attack again.

claims.claim: Players experience severe server latency, rubberbanding, and combat desync where local actions do not match server registration.

citations.review_text:
1/10 Stars: The Isle – Powerpoint Presentation Simulator
If you’ve ever wanted to experience what it feels like to play a survival game on a dial-up connection from 1999 while your router actively catches fire, The Isle is the game for you.

I didn't realize I was buying a turn-based strategy game, but that’s exactly what you get. You spend two hours meticulously growing a dinosaur, only to get killed by the ultimate apex predator: 3,000ms latency.

The Experience:
Rubberbanding Extravaganza: You press 'W' to walk forward, and the server decides to telepathically launch you backward off a cliff into the jaws of a Deinosuchus that wasn't even rendered two seconds ago.

Combat? What Combat? Fighting in this game is just two lag-teleporting lizard models violently phasing through each other while both players scream at their monitors. You don't win fights by skill; you win by having your lag-ghost desync more aggressively than the other guy's.

Pounce Mechanics: Playing a Raptor is great if you enjoy hitting a pounce, freezing in mid-air for four seconds, and teleporting directly into the stomach of whatever you were trying to attack.

Bottom Line:
The developers spent all their time making hyper-detailed dinosaur models, but apparently host their servers on a potato wired to a lemon.

Don't buy it unless you enjoy watching a slideshow of your own tragic death.

Update: Thank you steam for reminding me to update my review. Despite my attempts at trying to like this game and enjoy it, now I'm crashing almost repeatedly. Interesting that after playing over 40 hours on the previous update without a single crash, now on this latest patch I'm crashing non-stop. Add on the complaints below about the rain/fog and night time... Unplayable currently. 1/10. Without the crashing I'd have to put this to a 2/10. I think I've grasped more of what's going on when I die suddenly even though I'm nowhere near my enemy - I believe the online/replication of what's going on client side is showing something different than server side. For example as a raptor I see myself climb onto the back of what I am fighting, but then a few frames later I'm suddenly dead. It's as if my actions locally check out, but upon registering with the server - I am too late and I did not in fact lunge/pounce successfully. This 'lag' is unacceptable for an online game in 2026. 

It seems development is more focused on trying to make this as 'realistic' as possible instead of making it as 'fun' as possible. This is a game after all and the overwhelming urge of developers pushing more and more realism and forcing it down throats as 'fun' is unfortunate. The most recent update introduced heavy rain/fog making it even more difficult to see as well as darkening night time. I get it, day/night cycles are super 'fun' but honestly I don't enjoy waiting on storm or daylight to play the actual game.

The combat is fun when it's not buggy or laggy, I mostly played unofficial servers as official servers take incredibly long to grow/mature and randomly wipe your dinosaurs - awesome. That being said a lot of unofficial servers have mega/mixpacks of all kinds of carnivores/herbivores breaking any realism that the developer attempted to introduce not to mention all the typical online ego type of gameplay observed. Herbivores chasing down a lone carnivore to the edge of the map, groups…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe dying as resulting in the loss of hours of progress spent growing a dinosaur, noting that growing a large dinosaur takes many hours.

citations.review_text: Grow a giant croc for 8 hours rewarded with death by starvation

Spent 12 hours growing a Deino just to get pinned by a Rex and watch helplessly as my character does nothing while I die. The atmosphere is genuinely gorgeous, best dino legs in gaming, but the grind is basically a part time job with no pay and the game crashes more than my will to live. Growing up takes forever, food is scarce and dying means starting the whole nightmare over again. Getting grabbed with zero counterplay feels less like a mechanic and more like a personal attack. Fun with friends for maybe a weekend, then it becomes a chore. Not recommended, unless you enjoy suffering as a hobby.
[b][6/10][/b]

The Isle is one of the most immersive dinosaur survival games available. Instead of rushing players with quests or constant action, it focuses on survival, patience, and the feeling of living as a dinosaur. Every decision matters—from finding food and water to avoiding predators and choosing when to fight or flee.

The atmosphere is where the game truly shines. Dense forests, open plains, and realistic sound design create constant tension. You never know if another player is watching from the trees or if a larger predator is just over the next hill. Growing your dinosaur from a vulnerable juvenile into a fully grown adult makes every moment feel rewarding because death means losing hours of progress.

The gameplay isn't for everyone. Growth can be slow, and there are long periods where you're simply exploring, hunting, or hiding. Performance issues, bugs, and occasional balance problems can also be frustrating, especially after updates. New players may find the learning curve steep without guidance from friends or the community.

Despite its flaws, The Isle delivers an experience that few survival games can match. The player interactions, unpredictable encounters, and constant sense of danger create memorable stories every time you play. If you enjoy realistic survival games and don't mind a slower pace, The Isle is absolutely worth trying.

Rating: 9/10

Original:

Don't buy this on sale. Don't buy it at full price. Too many issues. The rubber-banding is next level. Your progress resets every day because of a "bug" that has never actually been addressed by the developers. Some of the playable dinosaurs can take well over 10 hours to grow to full adulthood. It is a shame because this game has so much potential. 

Yes, I have nearly 500 hours on the game. I clearly enjoy pain and torture.

** 7/11/26: **

The daily reset bug that was occurring in the official servers appears to have been fixed. A developer actually communicated with the Discord community and explained what happened. It would be nice if that was a normal thing. :)

I still have trouble recommending this game. Every new content update introduces bugs that compound with the ones that have already existed (in some case for YEARS). The rubber-banding and ultra-high ping spikes in the official servers seem to be normalized at this point. I have lost 2 dinos in the last few days alone because the game crashed on my PC and aggressive players took advantage of it. I expect this to happen every once in awhile but seems to be more common since the latest update.

The Isle Evrima is a lot of fun when it works. The latest Gateway map is very pretty and the Kentrosaurus (new playable) has introduced interesting game dynamics into the ecosystem. My recommendation for any new players is to join the official The Isle Discord and find others to play with. There are also unofficial servers to explore that offer unique rules, skin customization, community events, and more.

citations.review_text:
The new update has some good improvements, but the new skin creation system is a big step backward in my opinion. It feels much more restrictive and less enjoyable to use than the previous system. Creating a unique dinosaur is harder, and the customization options don’t feel as satisfying.

I hope the developers consider improving the skin system by adding more freedom, better color control, and more customization options. I really enjoy the game and want the skin creator to be as fun as the rest of the experience.

I love the game so much but omg the new color system that came out today is so ASS, the new patterns are really cool but the new colors are so limited and so very much boring. Makes everyone feel so similar because the colors are so simplified... I was already sad when they took away blues and purples for the hipsy but now this? I want my cool black/grey and white raptor back with his cool teal male marking!! Bring back the old color system! Literally everyone ive talk to hates the new color system!

Unfortunately, because of the most recent update [as of July 3rd, 2026], I no longer have a desire to truly play this game. The removal of the most pivotal mutation, Traumatic Thrombosis [something that prevents bleeding out to death when sitting], and the Skin System being trashed the way it has, has removed playability in general.

All skins and themes are now just limited nightmares. Each theme is limited to the tiniest amount of coloration change, with no saturation, and no brightness. It's all the same. Every skin will not look the same, each dinosaur having no unique variety in there colors, and all limited now to the same. Nothing will be visually distinct, and now the Primary reason i kept playing has been removed. 

Unless this skin system is reverted, or the themes are actually given distinct palettes to work with, such like the system prior to this update, instead of a gradient map that does nothing whatsoever, then I'll likely stop playing.
